pr_title: [C-API] Decimal casting to other type fixes
pr_body:
This PR fixes #4506 

In the C-API Decimals are not being treated as the correct internal type, and the `width` and `scale` of the decimal is not taken into account at all.

Bridges/adapters are built+tested for the following cast operations:

## Cast from DECIMAL

- [x] DECIMAL -> DOUBLE
- [x] DECIMAL -> FLOAT
- [x] DECIMAL -> VARCHAR
- [x] DECIMAL -> HUGEINT
- [x] DECIMAL -> BIGINT
- [x] DECIMAL -> UBIGINT
- [x] DECIMAL -> INTEGER
- [x] DECIMAL -> UINTEGER
- [x] DECIMAL -> SMALLINT
- [x] DECIMAL -> USMALLINT
- [x] DECIMAL -> TINYINT
- [x] DECIMAL -> UTINYINT

## Cast to DECIMAL

- [x] DOUBLE -> DECIMAL
- [x] FLOAT -> DECIMAL
- [x] VARCHAR -> DECIMAL
- [x] HUGEINT -> DECIMAL
- [x] BIGINT -> DECIMAL
- [x] UBIGINT -> DECIMAL
- [x] INTEGER -> DECIMAL
- [x] UINTEGER -> DECIMAL
- [x] SMALLINT -> DECIMAL
- [x] USMALLINT -> DECIMAL
- [x] TINYINT -> DECIMAL
- [x] UTINYINT -> DECIMAL

## Still missing

DECIMAL -> DECIMAL
pr_comments: It seems that `deprecated_duckdb_translate_column()` always writes DECIMAL into an array of hugeint. Maybe there is no need to distinguish the internal type? This is just my opinion, not necessarily correct.

> It seems that `deprecated_duckdb_translate_column()` always writes DECIMAL into an array of hugeint. Maybe there is no need to distinguish the internal type? This is just my opinion, not necessarily correct.

Ah I see, you're right, I missed that.

It also makes sense, because if you want to do anything with this result as a user in C, it's better to have it in a standard format.
Hmm it does appear to make a difference when casting
```
(lldb) p str
(char *) $0 = 0x0000000107451640 "1844674407370955161.1"
(lldb) p ff
(double) $1 = 1.8446744073709553E+18
```

Since the `decimal_to_double` tests are now dying, I'm thinking that the values are laid out in memory as 128 bits, but they are only occupying their respective 16,32,64,128 bits

So I now know what this old code was doing, it was fetching internal values, but that's not what `duckdb_value_...` is supposed to do right?
What I mean by internal values is fetching one to one, no conversions between what the type actually *is* and what is requested.
Looking at `result-c.cpp:224` and CDecimalConverter<T> it seems like it should not be necessary to fetch them as their internal types (int16_t, int32_t, etc..) but from what I tested it does?

There's something weird going on in prepared statements with DECIMAL
The created plan for binding `634.3453::DECIMAL(7,4)` into the prepared statement: `SELECT CAST($1 AS BIGINT)` in `client_context.cpp:305` is:
```
(lldb) p planner.plan->Print()
┌───────────────────────────┐
│         PROJECTION        │
│   ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─   │
│   CAST(0.0634 AS BIGINT)  │
└─────────────┬─────────────┘                             
┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
│         DUMMY_SCAN        │
└───────────────────────────┘    
```
EDIT:
It's not a bug in there, it's caused by `duckdb_double_to_hugeint` truncating, which.. makes sense

Ah that makes sense, but since we have things like `duckdb_decimal` which we expose to the user on the C side, we'll still need most of these changes, no?

Most of this code is just using the existing C++ operators but wrapping them to cast to the `duckdb_decimal` struct

I don't think we want to add `duckdb_value_decimal_as_properties` and I think having `duckdb_value_decimal` return 0 if the value is not a decimal seems acceptable to me. The reason `duckdb_value_decimal` exists is to allow for lossless fetching of decimal values - which only applies when the column type is decimal. I don't think it makes much sense to support using this in conjunction with columns of any other type, especially since the code to handle that seems to be quite involved.

issue_context.title: Invalid float-point literal handling in statements like 'SELECT -0.5;'
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

Hi!

I've spotted something that seems to be a HUGE bug in number handling. 

### To Reproduce

Try the following code:

```c++
duckdb_database db;
duckdb_connection con;

assert(duckdb_open(nullptr, &db) == DuckDBSuccess);
assert(duckdb_connect(db, &con) == DuckDBSuccess);

duckdb_result result;
assert(duckdb_query(con, "SELECT -0.5;", &result) == DuckDBSuccess);

auto type = duckdb_column_type(&result, 0);
auto ff = duckdb_value_double(&result, 0, 0); // 1.8446744073709552E+19
auto str = duckdb_value_varchar(&result, 0, 0); // "18446744073709551611"
```

If we execute a simple query `SELECT -0.5;` the value is treated as a DECIMAL. If I try getting this value as a double, I get a very strange value of 1.8446744073709552E+19. If I try getting this value as a VARCHAR, I get "18446744073709551611". 

If I try to explicitly specify the value type (i.e. `SELECT -0.5::DOUBLE;`), I get the correct value for all of the calls. If I try `SELECT 0.5;` query, I get just `5` for a double and `"5"` for a VARCHAR.

### OS:

macOS

### DuckDB Version:

v0.4.0, da9ee49

### DuckDB Client:

C++

### Full Name:

Ivan Drozdov

### Affiliation:

SMTU

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree
comments:
I think the issue here is this:
```c++
	case DUCKDB_TYPE_DECIMAL:
		return TryCastCInternal<hugeint_t, RESULT_TYPE, OP>(result, col, row);
```
DECIMAL can have different underlying physical types, here it is always assumed to be `hugeint_t`

> @Tishj It seems that TryCast::Operation doesn't handle scale like TryCastFromDecimal/StringCastFromDecimal does, which results in
> 
> ```c++
> query("SELECT 0.5::DECIMAL(18, 1)");
> duckdb_value_double(...) // get value 5
> ```

Yes I'm currently working on a fix ;)

```
(lldb) p ff
(double) $0 = -0.5
```
seems to actually be working now
for varchar it's still failing though
```
(lldb) p str
(char *) $1 = 0x0000000000000000
```

Eureka!
```
(lldb) p str
(char *) $0 = 0x0000000104f1bff0 "-0.5"
(lldb) p ff
(double) $1 = -0.5
```
still hitting the Allocator assertion though, so I'm not sure what's happening
